title: Yamada Nagamasa in Siam, c. 1612–1630
summary: A palanquin bearer from Numazu, it is said, who settled in Ayutthaya about 1612, rose to head its Japanese quarter, went to Japan in 1624 for a Red Seal permit, came back in 1627, and in 1630 was made governor of Ligor and poisoned in the succession struggle after King Songtham died.

legs.source: Yamada Nagamasa (Wikipedia): settled in Ayutthaya about 1612; the port he left from is not in the source
legs.note: Nagasaki is the usual Japanese port for Red Seal ships to Siam, not stated in the source.

legs.source: Yamada Nagamasa (Wikipedia): in Japan 1624 to 1627, seeking a Red Seal permit
Yamada Nagamasa (Wikipedia): back in Siam after 1627
Yamada Nagamasa (Wikipedia): made governor of Ligor (Nakhon Si Thammarat) in 1630

events.label: Ban Yipun, the Japanese quarter
events.text: About a thousand people lived in the Japanese village of Ayutthaya: traders, Christian converts and former samurai. He headed it from 1617.

events.label: Alleged privateering near Batavia
events.doubt: The privateering is alleged, not documented in the source read; the tales of treasure buried in Australia, told of him, the same article calls highly unlikely.
events.text: He is alleged to have attacked Dutch ships near Batavia.
